documents.harbor:
# Harbor service runbook

The harbor service listens on TCP port 8443 behind the internal load balancer.
Its break-glass admin account is svc-harbor-admin; rotate its key after use.
The maintenance window is every Tuesday from 02:00 to 04:00 UTC.
Incident escalation goes to the platform on-call rotation named tidewatch.
documents.scope:
# Rules of engagement

In scope: the 10.20.0.0/24 network and the web application at app.example.test.
Out of scope: the payment processing hosts in 10.20.5.0/28 and every third-party SaaS
provider. Denial-of-service and load testing are prohibited.

Testing may run on weekdays between 18:00 and 06:00 local time. The client's security
lead, Maya Chen, must be told before any exploitation attempt and can be reached on
+1 555 0100 around the clock.
documents.access:
# Access procedure

Operators authenticate with a hardware credential (a YubiKey) before access to the
jump host bastion-01. SSH keys for the jump host rotate every 90 days, and the
break-glass accounts are stored in the team vault under ops/breakglass.
Shared accounts are not permitted; every session is recorded.
documents.network:
# Network notes

The VPN concentrator vpn.example.test accepts IKEv2 on UDP 500 and 4500; remote
staff connect through it to reach the internal segments. Split tunnelling is disabled.

Internal DNS is served by ns1.corp.example.test and ns2.corp.example.test. The
staging environment mirrors production except that it has no customer data and uses
self-signed certificates.

Kafka brokers run on kafka-01 to kafka-03 on port 9092 with SASL/SCRAM. The Postgres
primary is db-01 on port 5432, replicated to db-02 in the second availability zone.
Nightly database backups are written to s3://corp-backups-eu with 35 days retention.

The monitoring stack is Prometheus on mon-01 scraping every 30 seconds, with Grafana
dashboards at grafana.corp.example.test. Alert routing sends paging alerts to the
on-call engineer and everything else to the #ops-alerts channel.
documents.findings:
# 2025 assessment findings

1. CVE-2025-12345 in the customer login portal allowed session fixation; patched in
   release 4.2.
2. SQL injection in the /api/v2/orders endpoint through the sort parameter; the
   developers moved to parameterised queries.
3. The legacy mail relay legacy-mail.example.test still accepted TLS 1.0.
4. Default credentials on two printers in the 10.20.0.0/24 range.
documents.deploy:
# Deployment guide for the orders platform

## Overview
The orders platform is a set of Python services behind an nginx ingress. Releases are
cut from the main branch every Thursday and promoted to production on Monday after the
change advisory board approves them. Hotfixes may skip the board with approval from the
duty manager.

## Build
Images are built by the CI pipeline and pushed to registry.corp.example.test/orders.
Every image is signed with cosign using the key in the vault path ops/cosign; unsigned
images are rejected by the admission controller in every cluster.

## Configuration
Runtime configuration lives in the orders-config repository. Secrets are never stored
there; the services read them at start-up from the vault agent sidecar. Feature flags
are served by the flagd service and default to off for new flags.

## Rollback
To roll back, redeploy the previous image tag with the deploy tool: `deployctl rollback
orders --to <tag>`. Database migrations are forward-only, so a rollback that crosses a
schema change needs the data team. Rollbacks must be announced in #orders-release.

## Observability
Service logs ship to the Loki cluster and are retained for 14 days. Traces are sampled
at 5 percent and sent to Tempo. The orders dashboard in Grafana shows request rate,
error rate and p99 latency per endpoint; paging alerts fire when the error rate stays
above 2 percent for ten minutes.

## Capacity
Each orders service runs three replicas per zone. Autoscaling adds replicas when CPU
stays above 70 percent for five minutes, up to twelve replicas per zone. The Postgres
connection pool is limited to 40 connections per replica to protect the primary.

## Contacts
The orders team owns the services; their lead is Priya Raman. The platform team owns
the clusters and the ingress. Security questions go to the application security channel.
